message.content: No, such discrete random variables do not exist. The reason is elementary. If a discrete random variable has a finite expectation, then its positive part has finite sum. Its negative part also has finite sum. Therefore its absolute value has finite expectation. This is the definition of integrability. Now suppose both X and Y are discrete random variables. Assume E(X) is finite. Assume E(Y) is finite. Then X is integrable. Then Y is integrable. The sum of integrable random variables is integrable. Thus X plus Y has finite absolute expectation. That expectation cannot be undefined. That expectation cannot be infinite. Moreover, the linearity rule applies. We may write E(X plus Y) as E(X) plus E(Y). Both terms on the right are finite numbers. Their sum is therefore a finite number. This conclusion holds for all discrete random variables. It does not depend on joint independence. It does not depend on correlation or dependence either. The key point is that finite expectations for each discrete variable prevent any hidden divergence or unbounded cancellation that could otherwise make the combined expectation fail to exist or become undefined or infinite beneath the assumptions.
